bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to agriculture; establishing the Office of Business Regulation and Land Ownership within the Department of Agriculture; requiring reports; appropriating money; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 17.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[17.034] OFFICE OF BUSINESS REGULATION AND LAND OWNERSHIP.

Subdivision 1.

Establishment.

The Office of Business Regulation and Land Ownership is established within the Department of Agriculture. The Office of Business Regulation and Land Ownership has the duties described in subdivision 2.

Subd. 2.

Duties; reports.

(a) The office must:

(1) examine the establishment of monopolies and consolidation of agriculture-related businesses in the state, including businesses that produce or sell agricultural commodities, seed, and agricultural chemicals;

(2) evaluate purchases of agricultural land and land consolidation across industries in the state by:

(i) individuals;

(ii) limited liability companies;

(iii) corporations;

(iv) churches; and

(v) other nonprofit organizations;

(3) identify trends in agricultural land purchasing and land consolidation across industries in the state; and

(4) provide advice to the commissioner of agriculture.

(b) The office must submit a biennial report with its findings to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with jurisdiction over agriculture.

Subd. 3.

Director; other staff.

(a) The commissioner of agriculture must appoint a director to manage the Office of Business Regulation and Land Ownership. The director must have knowledge about antitrust law, property law, and agriculture-related businesses. The director serves in the unclassified service.

(b) The commissioner must hire staff, including lawyers and economists, to perform the duties of the Office of Business Regulation and Land Ownership. The staff are in the unclassified service of the state. Compensation for staff must be established pursuant to chapter 43A. The staff must be reimbursed for the expenses necessarily incurred in the performance of official duties in the same manner as other state employees.

Sec. 2. APPROPRIATION; OFFICE OF BUSINESS REGULATION AND LAND OWNERSHIP.

$....... in fiscal year 2027 is appropriated from the general fund to the commissioner of agriculture for the purposes of establishing and funding the Office of Business Regulation and Land Ownership within the Department of Agriculture.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[17.034] OFFICE OF BUSINESS REGULATION AND LAND OWNERSHIP.

Subdivision 1.

Establishment.

The Office of Business Regulation and Land Ownership is established within the Department of Agriculture. The Office of Business Regulation and Land Ownership has the duties described in subdivision 2.

Subd. 2.

Duties; reports.

(a) The office must:

(1) examine the establishment of monopolies and consolidation of agriculture-related businesses in the state, including businesses that produce or sell agricultural commodities, seed, and agricultural chemicals;

(2) evaluate purchases of agricultural land and land consolidation across industries in the state by:

(i) individuals;

(ii) limited liability companies;

(iii) corporations;

(iv) churches; and

(v) other nonprofit organizations;

(3) identify trends in agricultural land purchasing and land consolidation across industries in the state; and

(4) provide advice to the commissioner of agriculture.

(b) The office must submit a biennial report with its findings to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with jurisdiction over agriculture.

Subd. 3.

Director; other staff.

(a) The commissioner of agriculture must appoint a director to manage the Office of Business Regulation and Land Ownership. The director must have knowledge about antitrust law, property law, and agriculture-related businesses. The director serves in the unclassified service.

(b) The commissioner must hire staff, including lawyers and economists, to perform the duties of the Office of Business Regulation and Land Ownership. The staff are in the unclassified service of the state. Compensation for staff must be established pursuant to chapter 43A. The staff must be reimbursed for the expenses necessarily incurred in the performance of official duties in the same manner as other state employees.

$....... in fiscal year 2027 is appropriated from the general fund to the commissioner of agriculture for the purposes of establishing and funding the Office of Business Regulation and Land Ownership within the Department of Agriculture.
